note.explanation: Torque tells us how strongly a force tends to turn an object. It depends on both the size of the force and its moment arm. For example, a door is easier to open when you push at its handle rather than near its hinge. A spanner turns a nut more easily when you apply force farther from the nut.
examples: A door handle is placed far from the hinge so a smaller force can turn the door.
A force of 400 N applied at the end of a 0.25 m spanner produces a torque of 100 N m.
note.simple: Torque is the turning effect of a force. A bigger force or a longer moment arm gives a greater turning effect.
note.checkQuestion: A force of 20 N acts perpendicularly at a moment arm of 0.4 m. What is the moment arm?
note.title: Torque and the moment arm
steps: Identify the force and its perpendicular distance from the axis.
Multiply the force by the moment arm.
Give the torque in newton metres (N m).
note.answer: Torque is the product of the force and the moment arm: τ = F × ℓ.

mcqs.stem: What is the magnitude of the torque when a force acts perpendicularly to its moment arm?
rationales: This is correct because torque is the product of force and moment arm.
This is incorrect because torque is not found by dividing force by moment arm.
This is incorrect because the moment arm is not divided by force.
This is incorrect because force multiplied by time is not the definition of torque.

options: The distance from the axis to the point where the force is applied
The perpendicular distance from the line of action of the force to the axis of rotation
The length of the rotating object
The distance travelled by the object
mcqs.stem: Which statement describes the moment arm of a force?
rationales: This is not always the moment arm because the distance must be perpendicular to the line of action.
This is correct because the moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the force’s line of action to the axis.
This is incorrect because the object's full length need not be the perpendicular distance.
This is incorrect because the moment arm is a distance from the axis, not the distance travelled.

options: The force acts at the greatest distance from the axis
mcqs.stem: When is the torque of a force zero?
rationales: This is not the only condition for zero torque; a non-zero force can also have zero torque.
This is correct because torque is zero when the moment arm is zero.
This is incorrect because torque does not become zero merely because the body has no mass.
This is incorrect because a greater moment arm generally gives greater torque.

mcqs.stem: According to the sign convention in this section, which torque is positive?
rationales: This is incorrect because clockwise torque is taken as negative.
This is correct because a force tending to produce anticlockwise rotation gives positive torque.
This is incorrect because a particular torque is assigned a direction according to the rotation it tends to produce.
This is incorrect because a force can produce a turning effect in either rotational direction.

options: Two equal and opposite parallel forces acting at different points
Two equal forces acting at the same point in the same direction
One force acting through the axis of rotation
Two unequal forces acting along the same line
mcqs.stem: Which pair of forces forms a couple?
rationales: This is correct because equal and opposite parallel forces at different points form a couple.
This is incorrect because forces at the same point in the same direction do not form a couple.
This is incorrect because one force through the axis is not a pair of forces forming a couple.
This is incorrect because a couple consists of equal and opposite parallel forces.

mcqs.stem: What is the SI unit of torque?
rationales: This is incorrect because the newton is the unit of force, not torque.
This is correct because torque is force multiplied by distance, so its SI unit is newton metre.
This is incorrect because metre per second is a unit of speed.
This is incorrect because kilogram metre is not the SI unit of torque.

written.text: A spanner 25 cm long is used to open a nut. If a force of 400 N is applied at the end of a spanner shown in Fig. 4.10, what is the torque acting on the nut?

rubric.why: The length must be expressed in metres for the SI torque unit.
rubric.description: Convert the spanner length to metres.

rubric.why: The torque relation is the required method.
rubric.description: Use the torque formula and substitute the values.
rubric.how: Write τ = F × ℓ and substitute 400 N and 0.25 m.

rubric.why: The final value and unit complete the numerical answer.
rubric.how: Calculate 400 × 0.25 and state the result in N m.

modelAnswer: Length of spanner ℓ = 25 cm = 0.25 m

written.text: Q4.3. What is the line of action of a force?
written.finalAnswer: The line along which the force acts is called the line of action of the force.

rubric.why: The definition must identify the line associated with the force.
rubric.how: Say that it is the line along which the force acts.

rubric.why: The answer must connect that line directly to the force.
rubric.how: Complete the definition by stating that the force acts along this line.

modelAnswer: The line along which the force acts is called the line of action of the force.

written.text: Q4.4. Define moment of a force. Prove that τ = rF sinθ, where θ is angle between r and F.
written.finalAnswer: Moment of a force is the product of the force and the moment arm; τ = rF sinθ.

rubric.why: The definition of moment of force is needed before the proof.
rubric.how: State that it is the product of the force and the moment arm.

rubric.why: Only the component of force perpendicular to r produces the turning effect.
rubric.description: Identify the perpendicular component of force.
rubric.how: Use the perpendicular component F sinθ.

rubric.why: Combining the perpendicular component with the distance gives the required relation.
rubric.description: Show the torque relation and state the result.
rubric.how: Use τ = r × F sinθ and simplify to τ = rF sinθ.

modelAnswer: Moment of a force or torque is defined as the product of the force and the moment arm.
The component of F perpendicular to r is F sinθ.

written.text: Q4.2. A force of 300 N is applied perpendicularly at the knob of a door to open it as shown in the given figure. If the knob is 1.2 m away from the hinge, what is the torque applied? Is it positive or negative torque?

rubric.why: The torque formula is the correct method for a perpendicular force.
Correctly identifying both given values is needed for substitution.
rubric.description: Substitute the force and moment arm.
rubric.how: Use F = 300 N and ℓ = 1.2 m.

rubric.why: Both the magnitude, unit and sign are required for the complete answer.
rubric.description: State the torque and its sign.
rubric.how: Calculate 300 × 1.2 and give the positive torque as indicated by the exercise answer.

written.text: Q4.6. A 30 cm long spanner is used to open the nut of a car. If the torque required for it is 150 N m, how much force F should be applied on the spanner as shown in the figure given below.

rubric.why: The moment arm must be in metres to use the SI units consistently.
rubric.description: Convert the spanner length to metres.

rubric.why: Rearranging the torque relation gives the required force.
rubric.description: Rearrange the torque formula and substitute.
rubric.how: Use F = τ ÷ ℓ with τ = 150 N m and ℓ = 0.30 m.

rubric.why: The calculated force with its unit is the required final answer.
rubric.how: Calculate 150 ÷ 0.30 and state the answer in newtons.

modelAnswer: Length of spanner ℓ = 30 cm = 0.30 m

examTips: Expect short questions asking for the definitions of line of action, moment arm, torque or couple. Learn the textbook definitions accurately.
For torque numericals, write τ = F × ℓ, show the force and moment arm with units, and give the answer in N m.
Convert lengths from centimetres to metres before calculating torque.
When asked for the sign, state whether the force tends to cause clockwise or anticlockwise rotation; anticlockwise is positive and clockwise is negative.
For a force at an angle, identify the perpendicular force component or perpendicular moment arm before using the torque relation.

hints: Use the torque formula for a force acting perpendicularly.
Multiply 300 N by the 1.2 m moment arm, then state the sign given in the exercise answer.

explain.title: Rigid body and axis of rotation
explain.body: If the distance between two points of the body remains the same under the action of a force, it is called a rigid body. During rotation, the body turns about an axis of rotation.

explain.title: Line of action and moment arm
explain.body: The line along which the force acts is called the line of action of the force. The perpendicular distance of the line of action of a force from the axis of rotation is known as moment arm of the force or simply moment arm.

explain.title: Moment of force or torque
explain.body: Moment of a force or torque is defined as the product of the force and the moment arm. Its magnitude is τ = F×ℓ, and its SI unit is newton metre (N m).

explain.title: Torque direction and couple
explain.body: Torque is positive if the force tends to produce an anticlockwise rotation and negative if it tends to produce a clockwise rotation. When two equal and opposite parallel forces act at two different points of the same body, they form a couple.

mistakes: Using the full distance to the point of force instead of the perpendicular moment arm.
Forgetting to change centimetres into metres before calculating torque.
Giving torque in newtons instead of newton metres (N m).
Mixing up the sign convention: anticlockwise is positive and clockwise is negative.
Forgetting that torque is zero if the line of action passes through the axis of rotation.
